BHARTIHEXA.why: The main driver is higher telecom revenue per user: mobile ARPU reached ₹252 in Q4 FY26 (₹242 a year earlier) and ₹259 in Q1 FY27. Home, office and other revenue (fixed wireless, broadband, IPTV) rose 65% in Q4, and leverage fell to 0.44x net debt to EBITDAaL. FY26 revenue rose 9.4% to ₹9,354 crore at a 54.2% EBITDA margin. The stock peaked in 2025 and has since given some back.
BHARTIHEXA.outlook: The case depends on further tariff increases and broadband growth. MOFSL assumed about 13% ARPU CAGR for FY24-27 (a 2025 note). The consensus target was about ₹1,868, with a range of ₹1,480-2,250. Valuation is high (P/E about 43-48) and Q4 profit figures differed across sources.

INDGN.why: Rose from about ₹483 in April 2026 to a ₹621.90 high on 25 September when Motilal Oswal upgraded it to Buy. Q1 FY27 revenue grew 39.7% to ₹1,063 crore. Brokers cite pharma outsourcing, its consulting-led model and rising AI use; 64% of revenue comes from the top 20 global drug companies.
INDGN.outlook: Motilal Oswal targets ₹708 (25x FY28 earnings) and expects revenue, EBIT and profit CAGRs of 19%, 29% and 27% over FY26-28, with EBITDA margin back to 19-20% by Q4 FY27. ICICI Securities has Add at ₹630. Simply Wall St's fair value is ₹490, below the recent price, and drug-company cost pressure and generative AI adoption are the swing factors.

TBOTEK.why: Growth in hotels: Q2 FY26 revenue rose about 26%, the Hotels and Ancillaries segment grew 20.4% and made up 64% of gross transaction value and 87% of gross profit, and monthly transacting buyers grew 8% led by international markets. The domestic business stabilised after a decline. The shares jumped over 11% on those results, but have been volatile (about -6% over a year to June 2026).
TBOTEK.outlook: Analyst consensus target was about ₹1,814 after Q2 FY26 (₹1,680-2,020); Motilal Oswal initiated at Buy with about 28% upside. Simply Wall St projects earnings growth of about 33-36% a year. A one-time ₹13 crore cost came from the Classic Vacations deal. Valuation is high and sources disagreed on the P/E.

IXIGO.why: Profit growth, not a straight rally: Q4 FY26 consolidated profit rose 91% to ₹32.1 crore and the shares rose about 6% in May 2026, but the stock had fallen from about ₹219 in January to roughly ₹171 in May and is down about 30% over six months to June. Q1 FY26 revenue had jumped 74% on train, bus and flight bookings.
IXIGO.outlook: JM Financial kept Buy but cut its target to ₹200. Earlier consensus expected FY26 revenue near ₹12.2 billion and EPS up 44%. Management plans to keep investing in technology and expand in non-metro cities. Valuation was a concern (P/E near 140 in January).

FIRSTCRY.why: Fell to record lows in 2026 on losses and margin pressure. Q3 FY26 net loss widened to ₹38.4 crore (from ₹14.7 crore) even as revenue rose 11.6% to ₹2,424 crore, and Q4 FY26 was another loss quarter. Causes cited: heavy discounting, weaker India profitability, and competition and last-mile costs (Ambit has a Sell rating). The stock is down about 56% over a year.
FIRSTCRY.outlook: Management reported FY26 profit-after-tax and free cash flow positive and said year-on-year revenue growth improved sequentially. Ambit says corrective steps are under way but recovery will take time. Only long-term investors were seen as candidates to accumulate.

UNIECOM.why: Fell after listing at ₹230 on the first day. No company-specific problem is evident: Q3 FY26 revenue grew 72% and Q1 FY27 profit rose 20.6% on 14% sales growth. One analysis blames foreign investor selling and a de-rating from a high listing valuation.
UNIECOM.outlook: FY26 annual report points to AI-led innovation in FY27. A partnership with Urban Company's Middle East arm (August 2026) puts Unicommerce's platform in UAE and Saudi operations. Third-party estimates expect double-digit revenue growth. The decline looks tied to valuation and sentiment more than weak results.

ORIENTTECH.why: Below its January 2025 high of ₹613 on weak FY26 profit: standalone profit before tax fell to ₹28.8 crore from ₹68.0 crore while revenue rose only about 3%. Management cited global supply-chain disruption in computers and data-centre hardware and the loss of a large hyperscaler cloud client. Q4 FY26 revenue fell 9% quarter on quarter. No single source tied these to the price directly.
ORIENTTECH.outlook: Order book for FY27 was about ₹400 crore in May 2026 and it won a ₹76.2 crore NPCI server order in July 2026. A report says Q1 FY27 returned to a ₹4.5 crore profit (verify in filings). Management is pushing managed services, device-as-a-service and cybersecurity for better margins.

PREMIERENE.why: Solar manufacturer riding policy-driven demand: module capacity went from 5.5 GW to 11.1 GW and cell capacity from 3.6 GW toward 10.6 GW by September 2026 under a ₹11,000 crore expansion (₹2,200 crore from IREDA). Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin was 30%, ahead of MOFSL's 27%. Q1 FY27 orders were ₹3,011 crore. The stock fell about 18% in 2025 before recovering.
PREMIERENE.outlook: Demand support: PM Surya Ghar (25-30 GW), PM Kusum (35 GW), CPSU phase II (12 GW) and the ALMM-2 rule for domestic cells. The company plans to integrate into ingots and wafers. One broker had Buy with a ₹1,195 target in May 2026. Capacity figures differed across sources.

KRN.why: Rallied about 500% in four months after the October 2024 listing and has stayed high. Q3 FY26 profit rose 65% to ₹23 crore on demand from data centres, exports and bus air-conditioning, supported by backward integration. Its heat exchangers serve data-centre cooling, commercial cooling and transport refrigeration.
KRN.outlook: Bull case: data-centre and export growth plus margin gains. Bear case: at a P/E of roughly 100-186 in 2026 (153.9 on 28 April) it has to keep delivering. It is also very volatile (about 4x Nifty). No broker targets or formal 2026 forecast were found.
